newsitem.title: UK: Formidable obstacles to UK joining 1999 EMU-Brown.
newsitem.headline: Formidable obstacles to UK joining 1999 EMU-Brown.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, launching a government guide to the European single currency aimed at businesses, said on Thursday there were "formidable obstacles" to British membership in 1999.

"The government's position on EMU (economic and monetary union) has not changed. While nothing has been ruled out, there are formidable obstacles to the United Kingdom joining on January 1, 1999," Brown said in a statement.
But he added: "Our aim is to help British companies make the most of opportunities in Europe. This means being ready for the single currency whether or not we join."
The guide describes what the single currency will mean for financial systems and accounts, computer systems and cash-handling procedures.
It warns businesses to think about the effects on their pricing strategies, marketing, relations with other firms and raising finance.
Brown announced he was setting up a group of business representatives to advise the government on the practical implications of the single currency.
He said he had written to the heads of about 20 organisations representing different sectors of the economy asking them to nominate an individual to sit on the panel.
